subject: HIPAA BAA availability and deployment eligibility - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <slopez@medcloud.health>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medcloud.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: HIPAA / BAA eligibility & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — great to get a clearer picture of MedCloud's workflows. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on PHI handling, what deployment modes are eligible, and the security artifacts you'll need.

Recap from today:
- Use case: routing clinical notes + patient identifiers through Redwood to generate clinical summaries and triage recommendations. You indicated PHI (names, MRNs, dates) will be included in prompts.
- Redwood capability: we can support HIPAA-covered workflows, but BAA-backed PHI processing is limited to isolation-capable deployments.

What we confirmed (high level):
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for customers processing PHI, but note the deployment modes that are eligible (see below).
- Eligible deployment modes for PHI under a signed BAA: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Hosted (shared multitenant API): not eligible for PHI / covered data. If you need a hosted-style experience, we can evaluate a dedicated-hosted pool as part of Dedicated offering.
- PHI boundaries: Any prompt or attached content containing identifiers (names, MRNs, SSNs, contact info) is considered PHI. Under a BAA we will treat those inputs as covered data and apply isolation, encryption, and logging controls per the agreement.

Security artifacts and next steps we committed to provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report / AOC (we will share a redacted copy).
- Draft BAA for review (attached).
- Answers to your vendor security questionnaire. Please send the questionnaire (or we can start one from our side) — I attached the draft BAA and noted the questionnaire file name I saw in the drive.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tom / Sara: Confirm that your production path will send PHI to Redwood (yes/no) and estimate volumes (monthly tokens / records).
2) MedCloud: please share your security questionnaire (or confirm the copy I should fill out).
3) Redwood: Dev will coordinate on the questionnaire and provide SOC2 AOC + redwood_baa_draft.pdf within ~5 business days.
4) Schedule a 30-min security call (availability: Tue/Wed morning PST) to review any technical boundary questions (key management, logs, retention).

Attachments:
- redwood_baa_draft.pdf (Draft BAA)

If that all looks right I'll start the questionnaire fill and loop in our legal team for the BAA timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security/compliance team before we kick off the questionnaire:

1) Hosted eligibility: You noted hosted is not eligible for PHI. Can you confirm whether any hosted endpoints are ever used for caching or telemetry where PHI could be inadvertently stored?

2) Encryption & key management: We use customer-managed keys (CMKs) in our cloud for sensitive workflows. Do you support CMEK or an integration with our KMS/HSM for Dedicated or Private deployments?

3) Retention & logs: What is Redwood's default retention for request logs and KV/prefix cache? Can these be configured/disabled under the BAA?

4) SOC 2: Please share the latest SOC 2 AOC + scope (which systems are in scope).

We'll attach our security questionnaire in our next email (Tom will upload). We're also interested in a timeline for BAA execution (legal review + signature).

Best,

Hi Sara — thanks for the questions, good ones. I asked Dev to jump in with technical answers; I'll also attach the SOC2 AOC and the BAA draft for your legal team.

Quick answers while Dev jumps in:
- Hosted telemetry: Redwood's hosted multitenant API does not provide PHI isolation guarantees and is therefore not approved for PHI. For customers processing PHI we route them to Dedicated or Private deployments where telemetry and logs for that tenant can be isolated and configured per the BAA.
- Timeline: typical timeline from questionnaire + legal review to signed BAA ranges from 1–3 weeks depending on redlines. We'll aim for 2 weeks for an initial signature if MedCloud can provide the questionnaire and legal contacts quickly.

Attachments included: redwood_baa_draft.pdf, SOC2-AOC-redwood-2027.pdf

Dev — tagging you for the technical answers below, especially CMEK, retention, and cache behavior.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <slopez@medcloud.health>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medcloud.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HIPAA / BAA eligibility & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks — happy to clarify from a technical standpoint. I'll answer inline to the numbered items Sara raised.

1) Hosted telemetry / accidental storage:
- Hosted (shared multitenant) endpoints do not have tenant-level isolation guarantees for telemetry and are not acceptable for PHI under our BAA. Any cached prefixes or intermediate telemetry in hosted will be shared infrastructure level and cannot be guaranteed not to contain identifiers. For PHI use cases we require Dedicated or Private.

2) Encryption & key management (CMEK / KMS / HSM):
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed keys (CMEK) using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault depending on region. Keys can be rotated per your key policy; we also support bringing your own key material (BYOK) in Private/on-prem deployments using HSM integrations.

3) Retention & logs / KV cache:
- Default: request logs and traces retained for 30 days; model input cache TTL depends on configuration (default 1 hour).
- Under a BAA: retention policies are configurable — we can reduce log retention, disable analytical telemetry, and set cache TTLs to zero for covered workloads. Persistent KV cache for acceleration is optional and can be disabled for PHI workloads.

4) SOC 2 scope / AOC:
- Attached is our SOC 2 Type II AOC (redacted) covering production inference runtime, control plane for Dedicated/Private, and access management. If you need additional evidence (penetration testing reports, network diagrams), we can schedule a security call and provide a scoped set of artifacts.

Other notes on PHI handling and boundary:
- Definition: PHI = any data that includes direct identifiers (name, MRN, DOB, SSN, contact info) or any combination that can reasonably re-identify a patient.
- Ingress/egress: we treat inputs as covered data under the BAA. Outputs that contain identifiers are also covered; customers remain responsible for redaction prior to sending if they prefer not to store identifiers.
- Model weights/privileged data: we do not train on customer-provided PHI; model updates in our hosted catalog are segregated from customer data for Dedicated/Private customers.

Next steps & timeline:
- If you can upload the security questionnaire (or confirm the file we should fill), I will begin completing it today and aim to return a completed copy + SOC2 AOC within 3 business days.
- Legal: once the questionnaire and standard BAA are in flight, legal review tends to be the pacing item. For many customers we reach signature in ~1–2 weeks.
- Proposed meeting: Wed 2027-09-15 10:00 AM PST (30m) — I'll send a calendar invite if that works.

Attachments referenced: redwood_baa_draft.pdf, SOC2-AOC-redwood-2027.pdf

Let me know if you'd like a short design doc on how we isolate keys and caches for Dedicated deployments — happy to provide.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
